title: ::: K-IG 교육 영어듣기훈련프로그램 | 기초2 | 제 001 회 강의 :::
label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 080 ]

blocks.text: That spring, I was taken to my first big-league game. Just as we approached the exit after the game, I caught sight of Willie Mays. He was standing near the gate not ten feet away from me. I rushed to him and said, “Mr. Mays, could I please have your autograph?” He said, “Sure, kid. You got a pencil?” I didn’t have one in my pocket. The great Willie Mays stood there watching in silence. He just shrugged and said, “Sorry, kid.” And then he walked out of the ballpark into the night. I didn’t want to cry, but tears started falling down my cheeks, and there was nothing I could do to stop them.

I was eight years old. At that moment in my life, nothing was more important to me than baseball. My team was the New York Giants, and I followed the doings of those men in the black-and-orange caps with all the devotion of a true believer. Even now, remembering that team, which no longer exists, I can recite the names of nearly every baseball player on the team. But none was greater, and none more perfect than Willie Mays.

After that night, I started carrying a pencil with me wherever I went. It became a habit of mine never to leave the house without making sure I had a pencil in my pocket. It’s not that I had any particular plans for that pencil, but I didn’t want to be unprepared. I had been caught empty-handed once, and I wasn’t about to let it happen again. If nothing else, the years have taught me this:If there’s a pencil in your pocket, there’s a good chance that one day you’ll feel tempted to start using it.

readingSentences.english: Each day each of us engages in many forms of complex activities.
readingSentences.korean: 매일 우리들 각자는 많은 형태의 복잡한 활동에 참가한다.

readingSentences.english: We go to school, participate in sports, drive cars, and often get involved in conflicts.
readingSentences.korean: 우리는 학교에도 가고, 운동에도 참가하고, 자동차도 몰고, 종종 갈등에 연루되기도 한다.

readingSentences.english: Why are some activities, like eating or reproducing, common to all organisms, while others, like building nests, are restricted to certain species?
readingSentences.korean: 왜 먹거나 번식하는 것과 같은 일부 활동들은 모든 유기체에 공통이지만, 둥지를 짓는 것과 같은 다른 활동들은 특정한 종들에만 제한될까?

readingSentences.english: Why do some animals live in groups and others live alone?
readingSentences.korean: 왜 일부 동물들은 무리를 지어서 살고 다른 동물들은 혼자 살까?

readingSentences.english: We also perform other, less complex activities such as eating and sleeping.
readingSentences.korean: 우리는 또한 먹거나 잠을 자는 것과 같은 덜 복잡한 활동도 수행한다.

readingSentences.english: Our nervous system determines the complexity of activities that we are able to perform.
readingSentences.korean: 우리의 신경계가 우리가 수행할 수 있는 활동들의 복잡성을 결정한다.

readingSentences.english: Animals with nervous systems similar to a worm’s cannot play soccer, much less chess.
readingSentences.korean: 벌레와 유사한 신경계를 가진 동물들은 축구를 할 수 없고 하물며 체스는 더더욱 할 수 없다.

readingSentences.english: Questions such as these are the focus of the study of behavior.
readingSentences.korean: 이러한 질문들이 행동 연구의 핵심 초점이다.

readingSentences.english: In its simplest form, behavior is the conduct of an organism―the way it acts.
readingSentences.korean: 가장 단순한 형태로 보면, 행동은 한 유기체의 행위, 즉 그것이 활동하는 방식이다.
